notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as the town reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by a separate school district. The town's tax bill also collects the taxes for the state education tax (which pays for schools) and the county; residents pay all of them, but only the town's share is counted here.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The town borrowed $1,510,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Debt service leaves out $290,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the town did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Vermont city, town and village candidates do not file campaign finance reports with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 1 license-plate camera is mapped inside Town of Bennington's borders in OpenStreetMap (1 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Vermont yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 1 Flock Safety license-plate camera is mapped inside Town of Bennington's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is not recorded; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
